html:
SMTO-TSK-0010 — A finished run's settings can't be changed

GUID: 32ce247e-9dd7-4161-96ea-2a350f363034
Slug: run-settings-historical
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • This run has already ended or been stopped, so its settings are kept as a record of how it ran. SMTO didn't change them.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In Agent Checks, change the scope from This run to This conversation or Global, then make your change. A finished run can't be changed, but these scopes apply your setting to the next tasks you start.
  2. Send a new message, or start the task again, so the new setting is used. New work picks up the updated setting, while the old run keeps its record unchanged.

What success looks like

  • The setting saves under the new scope and the next task you start uses it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't try to edit the finished run's record to change how it ran; it is kept as history.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A run-scoped settings edit was rejected because the run is already terminal (answered, completed, failed, cancelled or interrupted) or has a committed cancellation, and its captured settings are read-only history.

What this means

  • A current-run setting edit encounters a terminal status or a committed cancellation and rejects modification of captured history. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • A current-run setting edit encounters a terminal status or a committed cancellation and rejects modification of captured history.

How to diagnose it

  • Check terminal/cancellation state and distinguish historical snapshots from settings for future tasks.

How to fix it

  • Run-scoped edits are rejected once native_runs.status is terminal or a native_cancellations row exists. Leave the historical settings as they are; apply the new policy at conversation or global scope (or as a prompt override) for future tasks, or to a run that is still active.
  • Keep the historical record intact. Choose supported controls on the current run or configure a new task.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Historical settings remain intact and intended new behavior is configured through a supported current/future scope.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass the unsupported-feature check or reinterpret an unsupported response as success.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
